End of body: . No inline styles/scripts/handlers anywhere. BODY ORDER + IDS/CLASSES (BEM): 1. Skip to content 2.
Nick Salazar

text:
Palette confirmation from real shipped pixels + video specs (from media-preparation). Details: /Users/scottscheferman/nick-salazar-website/analysis/verification/media/palette-confirmation.md and palette.json (script extract-palette.py is re-runnable).

VIDEO SPECS: all 7 clips are 1168x768 (aspect 1.521:1, i.e. 73:48, near 3:2), 10.04 s, 24 fps, h264 High yuv420p, faststart, 2.2–7.5 MB. NO AUDIO STREAM in any shipped clip, so autoplay muted playsinline is safe with nothing to strip. Posters: poster-01/03–07 are 1920x1280 (3:2, 1.4 % aspect difference from the clip, hidden by object-fit: cover); poster-02-coils is 1168x768 native. New mobile set poster-0N-*-960.jpg (960x640, 88–118 KB). Photos hero.jpg + photo-*.jpg are 1920x1440 (4:3). Use width/height attributes accordingly.

MEASURED COLOURS (OKLab-gated, % of sampled pixels in the clip):
- signal-orange #F26B1C (oklch 0.703 0.184 47.6): CONFIRMED. Footage orange = 03-crane unit median #EC7D2F (oklch 0.703 0.160 51.1) 1.3 %; 04-drums straps #E27B29 2.6 %. Footage is slightly lighter/yellower than token; keep #F26B1C or nudge to #EE7A2E.
- signal-red #E5341E (oklch 0.616 0.213 30.8): CONFIRMED. 02-coils faces median #D22628 (oklch 0.567 0.202 27.6) 9.3 % (strongest single colour of any clip); 05 flat-racks turn red late (#BF565D). Footage red is deeper; #D9282A would sit on it exactly.
- signal-yellow #F2C81C (oklch 0.847 0.175 91.0): CONFIRMED STRONGLY. 07-yard units #F0C61D 11 %; 04-drums cylinders #EAB91C 7.7 %; 01-hero unit #E2BE20 3 %; 03 slings #E9C021. Token within 0.03 OKLab of measured.
- signal-sky #6FB4E2 (oklch 0.744 0.100 236.6): NOT EVIDENCED. 0 % in 01/02/03/04/07; 0.3 % in 05; 1.7 % only in 06-warehouse (blue film highlights, #7DACE2). The only blues in the plates are navy tarps 05 (#1D2D57, 16.6 %) and the blue film in 06 (#1658A1, 5.3 %), both too dark for text on dark ground. Real sky-blue exists only in photo-crane.jpg (#4C6899/#7695C2), i.e. the photo layer.

RECOMMENDATION for the credentials accent: signal-yellow (name orange, credentials yellow). Yellow is in 4/7 plates at the highest coverage and is ~40° from orange in OKLCH hue (orange ≈ 48–51°, yellow ≈ 91°), so the two stay distinct; red is only ~20° from orange and would blur. If a cool accent is still wanted, the only footage-derived blue is a lightened tarp blue ≈ #2F6FBF; label it tarp-blue, not sky.

Per-clip dominant chromatic hue (for plate-specific tinting): 01 yellow, 02 red, 03 orange(+red hook, yellow slings), 04 yellow(+orange straps), 05 navy blue(+red racks), 06 warm wood orange-brown + blue film, 07 yellow. Ask me if you want per-frame timelines or different thresholds.

Your load-bearing hooks are all present exactly as named: html.no-js; nav.nav[data-nav][aria-label=Primary] > a.nav__mark + ul.nav__links > li > a.nav__link[data-nav-link] ×4 + a.nav__cta.btn.btn--outline.btn--sm + details.nav__menu[data-nav-menu] > summary.nav__toggle + ul.nav__sheet; hero = section.plate.plate--hero#top[data-plate="01"][data-hero] > .plate__frame > .plate__media > video.plate__video[data-video][preload=metadata][poster] > source[src] (real src, hero only), .plate__shade, .hero__light, .plate__copy.hero__copy > p.hero__creds[data-reveal], h1.hero__name[data-reveal] > span.hero__line ×2, p.hero__role[data-reveal], a.btn.btn--outline.hero__cta[data-reveal]; six plates section.plate#plate-{coils,crane,drums,containers,warehouse,yard}[data-plate="02".."07"] with video[data-video][preload=none][poster] > source[data-src], .plate__shade, .plate__copy > h2.plate__pair (3 span.plate__word, exactly one .plate__word--accent per plate with data-accent: coils=red, crane=default orange, drums=yellow, containers=sky, warehouse=sky, yard=yellow) + div.plate__story[data-reveal] > p + p.plate__meta; text sections section.section#{credentials,services,work,why,contact} > .section__inner > h2.section__title + p.section__lede; dl.facts > div.facts__row[data-reveal] > dt.facts__term + dd.facts__desc (contains

s); form#brief-form.brief__form with div.field > label.field__label + .input (+ .input--area on textareas) + p.field__help#-help; pre#brief-output.brief__output[tabindex=0]; #brief-copy.btn.btn--fill, #brief-download.btn.btn--outline, p#brief-status.brief__status[role=status], p.brief__note; footer.foot#foot > p.foot__line + .foot__meta > span.foot__mark + span.foot__muted ×2. DELTAS you need to know (please style/bind these): 1. Script: at end of body (lead's markup rule). Module scripts are deferred by default, so your app.js runs after parse either way; just avoid top-level `this`. If you truly need a classic defer script, say so and I'll switch. 2. data-plate carries the number ("01".."07") instead of being bare; [data-plate] selectors still match. 3. Hero extras: p.hero__lede[data-reveal] (one short paragraph after .hero__role) and p.plate__meta inside .hero__copy ("Illustrative footage…"). Hero creds keep inner spans: span.hero__cred ×2 + span.hero__sep (aria-hidden) so you can give the creds their own accent; the h1 is the largest type, creds a DIFFERENT accent (lead rule). 4. Nav CTA text is "Build a brief" (lead's label). If it will not fit single-line beside 4 links at 320px, hide .nav__links at narrow widths and rely on the details menu; the CTA must stay one line. Nav link ids in order: #credentials, #work, #services, #contact. Full section order for highlighting: top, plate-coils, credentials, plate-crane, services, plate-drums, work, plate-containers, plate-warehouse, plate-yard, why, contact, foot. 5. Services: I used

    > li.services__item[data-reveal] > h3.services__name + p.services__desc and DROPPED .services__num. Reason: 14 numbered items reads as the "eyebrow on every section" tell (anti-patterns.md, gate 54 territory) and the list is not ordinal. Please style .services__list without numbers. 6. Credentials diptych: .creds__grid > .creds__text (dl.facts + p.creds__note) + figure.creds__figure[data-reveal] > img.creds__img (1920×1440, loading=lazy) + figcaption.creds__caption. Needs a two-column layout at ≥768 that collapses to one column below; image track must be minmax(0,1fr) (gate 50). 7. Work gallery: ul.work__grid > li.work__cell > figure.work__figure[data-reveal] > img.work__img (1920×1440, lazy) + figcaption.work__caption, six items. Needs your grid + caption styles. 8. Why section: .why__points > article.why__point[data-reveal] > h3.why__heading + p.why__text ×3. 9. Brief fields (ids load-bearing for your app.js): bf-service (select, 14 real services, first option value=""), bf-cargo (textarea), bf-where, bf-when, bf-evidence (textarea, NEW: "Evidence you need" — lead requirement), bf-name, bf-org, bf-contact (NEW: "How to reach you" — lead requirement, the reader's own contact details), bf-notes (textarea). Please include bf-evidence and bf-contact in the assembled brief text. Every control has aria-describedby="-help". 10. Footer is OUTSIDE main (after ), as HTML semantics require; your skeleton had it inside. .foot__meta has three spans: foot__mark, foot__muted (provenance/credentials note), foot__muted (©). 11. data-reveal count is 42 total; ≤8 per section except services (14 items) and work (6) — if 14 staggered reveals is too many, tell me and I'll move data-reveal to the ul. 12. media-preparation also ships 960-wide posters (assets/photos/poster-NN-*-960.jpg) if you want a narrow-viewport poster swap; the
